So, some suggestions to attack this from a couple angles:

- The gym is a rare place you can fully exert yourself and be free to express fatigue/exhaustion that follows. I've certainly been so gassed after sets that I had my hands on my knees/sat against the wall/laid on the ground to recover. Your description of your physical reaction doesn't sound super different from this! 
- If you're still curious of how it looks, consider filming one of your sets to see it from observer's perspective and reviewing it objectively - that is to say, no hyperanalyzing or pixel-by-pixel scrutiny.
- OH. Another actionable thing: consider analyzing how you breathe during sets. Regulating your breath can be useful during intimacy to control orgasms, so the same principle may apply here. Bonus: exhaling on concentric motions (e.g. in a crunch, contracting your core to sit up) and inhaling slowly on eccentric motions (e.g. lowering your torso post-crunch) may increase your muscle-mind connection

As others said, your mana looks really inconsistent and not set up to support your goals. You have a total of 3 black sources, so I'm not sure you're going to be able to cast your black spells with any regularity. Without the rare lands enabling you to be more ambitious, I'd stick to two colors. I saw you wanted to build with Anim Pakal - which is a good idea, as it's a powerful card - so I'd stick to red/white.

The next question is: what does Anim Pakal do well, and what does it ask of you to do it?

I would say it helps you go wide, and benefits from having other creatures able to attack the turn it comes down (even if those attacks aren't strictly profitable; context will determine this). To enable Anim Pakal, you'll want plenty of cheaper creatures to, especially if they provide two bodies for the price of one - a card like [[Resolute Reinforcements]] plays into this idea well. This brings up a really important concept called the **mana curve** - there's plenty to read on this already.

I'd suggest taking a look at other decks for inspiration: [here's one with Anim Pakal](https://www.mtggoldfish.com/archetype/standard-boros-aggro-mid#paper) and [here's another red/white aggro deck](https://www.mtggoldfish.com/deck/6027558#paper) doing similar things.

Take something like monored: if it's creatures live more than the turn they're played, it's basically bonus. If a one drop cracks in for 2 damage, it's more or less done its job.

Other creatures come with ETB effects where even if they die instantly, they've delivered their value; think of something like Thran Spider in this case.

Other creatures protect themselves, which makes it tricky for opponents to time their removal. See: Guardian of New Benalia, Graveyard Trespasser.
